name: AgentEvalSpec
description:
AgentEvalSpec says which agent version is evaluated, on which of its
 plugins' cases, on which models, how many times, and within what spend.

fields.name: AgentVersion
fields.description:
The agent version to evaluate, a version hash or a tag. Empty
 evaluates the current version.

fields.name: Plugins
fields.description:
The slugs of the plugins whose cases run, each one the agent
 attaches. Empty runs the cases of every plugin the agent attaches.

fields.name: Targets
fields.description:
The engines and models each case runs on, at most six. Empty runs
 each case on the agent as it runs: its own engine, model and settings.

fields.name: Runs
fields.description:
Tries per case and target, from 1 to 50. Zero uses each case's own
 runs value, or 3.

fields.name: Threshold
fields.description:
The score a case needs to pass, from 0 to 1, or 1 when unset: every
 scored check passes on every try.

fields.name: CaseGlob
fields.description:
Runs only the cases whose directory name matches this glob, as in
 "review-*". Empty runs every case.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description:
Runs only the cases carrying at least one of these tags. Empty runs
 every case.

fields.name: JudgeModel
fields.description:
The model AI-graded checks use. Empty uses the platform's default
 judge model.

fields.name: MaxCostUsd
fields.description:
The most this eval may spend, in estimated US dollars of model cost.

 Checked before each try starts, counting what tries already spent and
 the cap each running try still holds: tries already running and their
 AI-graded checks finish, so the spend can pass the limit by those.

fields.name: Concurrency
fields.description: Tries running at once, from 1 to 8. Zero means 1.

fields.name: AllowTools
fields.description:
Tools every try may use beyond each case's own list, in Claude Code's
 names, as Claude Code's --allow-tools.

 A try runs the agent with only the tools its case and this list grant,
 within the agent's own tool lists: name the agent's working tools here
 (Skill for its skills, Agent for its hand-offs to subagents). A
 specifier in parentheses, as in Bash(npm test *), grants the whole
 tool. A plugin's MCP tools are named either way: Claude Code's
 mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool> or Stigmer's
 mcp__<server>__<tool>.

fields.name: RealMcpServers
fields.description:
Runs the plugins' MCP servers for real, with the organization's
 connections. Off by default: a try cannot call the plugins' MCP tools,
 as in Claude Code's evals without mocks.

fields.name: Vaults
fields.description:
Vaults whose logins and secrets the tries use, in order: the first
 vault holding a match wins. At most 20.

 A try has no person, so these vaults are all its hooks and servers
 use. Each is a shared vault: a My vault, the creator's included, is
 refused, because every viewer of the agent may read a try, and a
 hook's or server's output can show what a key unlocked.

fields.name: SkipScaffold
fields.description:
Skips each case's scaffold script, as Claude Code's --no-scaffold; a
 case that has one is then listed as not run.

fields.name: AllowRealServers
fields.description:
Starts the plugins' real MCP servers for the servers no mock answers,
 as Claude Code's --allow-real-servers; mocked tools still answer from
 their files. Their tools still need allow_tools.
